title_en: Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning Property Investigation in Civil Enforcement

articles.content_en: Article 1: In the course of enforcement, the applicant for enforcement shall provide leads on the property of the party subject to enforcement; the party subject to enforcement shall truthfully report its property; the People's Court shall conduct investigation through the online enforcement inquiry and control system, and, where investigation through other means is necessary based on the needs of the case, shall adopt such other investigation methods at the same time.

Article 2: Where the applicant for enforcement provides leads on the property of the party subject to enforcement, it shall fill in a property investigation form. Where the property leads are clear and specific, the People's Court shall investigate and verify within seven days; where circumstances are urgent, it shall investigate and verify within three days. Where the property leads are confirmed, the People's Court shall promptly take corresponding enforcement measures.
Where the applicant for enforcement is truly unable to ascertain the property on its own due to objective reasons, it may apply to the People's Court for investigation.

Article 3: Where the People's Court, upon the application of the applicant for enforcement or ex officio, orders the party subject to enforcement to report its property, it shall issue a property reporting order to such party. In the enforcement of monetary claims, the property reporting order shall be issued simultaneously with the enforcement notice.
Where the People's Court, based on the needs of the case, orders the party subject to enforcement to report its property again, it shall issue a new property reporting order to such party.

Article 7: After the party subject to enforcement reports its property, if its property changes and such change affects the realization of the applicant for enforcement's claim, it shall submit a supplementary report to the People's Court within ten days from the date of the property change.

Article 8: The People's Court shall promptly investigate and verify the property reported by the party subject to enforcement, and may, when necessary, organize the parties to hold a hearing.
Where the applicant for enforcement applies to inquire into the property reported by the party subject to enforcement, the People's Court shall permit it. The applicant for enforcement and its agents shall keep confidential the information learned during the inquiry.

Article 9: Where the party subject to enforcement refuses to report, falsely reports, or fails to report its property within the time limit without justifiable reasons, the People's Court may, depending on the seriousness of the circumstances, impose a fine or detention on the party subject to enforcement or its legal representative; if the conduct constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.
Where a unit has committed any of the acts stipulated in the preceding paragraph, the People's Court may impose a fine or detention on its principal person in charge or directly responsible personnel; if the conduct constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 10: Where the party subject to enforcement refuses to report, falsely reports, or fails to report its property within the time limit without justifiable reasons, the People's Court shall, in accordance with relevant provisions, include it in the list of judgment debtors subject to credit punishment.

Article 12: Where the party subject to enforcement fails to perform the obligations determined in the effective legal instrument in accordance with the enforcement notice, the People's Court shall have the authority to investigate, through the online enforcement inquiry and control system, on-site investigation, or other means, the identity information and property information of the party subject to enforcement from the party, relevant entities, or individuals; the relevant entities and individuals shall provide assistance according to law.
The People's Court may copy, print, transcribe, photograph, or extract and retain in other manners the materials needed for investigation.
Where the applicant for enforcement applies to inquire into the property information investigated by the People's Court, the People's Court may decide whether to permit it based on the needs of the case. The applicant for enforcement and its agents shall keep confidential the information learned during the inquiry.

Article 13: An investigation conducted by the People's Court through the online enforcement inquiry and control system shall have the same legal effect as an on-site investigation.
Electronic legal instruments made by the People's Court in the course of investigation shall have the same legal effect as paper legal instruments; electronic inquiry results fed back by units assisting in enforcement shall have the same legal effect as paper feedback results.

Article 14: Where the party subject to enforcement conceals property, accounting books, or other materials and refuses to surrender them, the People's Court may take search measures according to law.
When the People's Court conducts a search according to law, if the party subject to enforcement is ordered to open the premises, boxes, cabinets, or other places or containers where the party may have concealed property or materials, but refuses to cooperate, the People's Court may forcibly open them.

Article 15: In order to ascertain the property status of the party subject to enforcement and its ability to perform obligations, the People's Court may summon the party subject to enforcement or its legal representative, person in charge, actual controller, or directly responsible personnel to the People's Court to accept investigation and inquiry.
Where the party subject to enforcement, its legal representative, person in charge, or actual controller who must accept investigation and inquiry, after being legally summoned, refuses to appear without justifiable reasons, the People's Court may summon them by force; where the whereabouts of the aforesaid persons are unknown, the People's Court may, in accordance with relevant provisions, notify relevant entities to assist in locating them.

Article 16: Where the People's Court has gone through the registration procedures for seizure of specific movable property of the party subject to enforcement, such as motor vehicles, ships, or aircraft, but has failed to actually impound such property, it may, in accordance with relevant provisions, notify relevant entities to assist in locating the property.

Article 17: Where a legal person or unincorporated organization that is the party subject to enforcement fails to perform the obligations determined in an effective legal instrument, and the applicant for enforcement believes that the party subject to enforcement has circumstances of evading debts such as refusing to report or falsely reporting property, concealing or transferring property, or that its shareholders or contributors have circumstances such as false capital contributions or withdrawal of capital contributions, the applicant may apply in writing to the People's Court to commission an audit institution to audit the party subject to enforcement. The People's Court shall decide whether to permit it within ten days from the date of receipt of the written application.

Article 18: Where the People's Court decides to conduct an audit, it shall randomly determine a qualified audit institution and order the party subject to enforcement to submit accounting vouchers, accounting books, financial accounting reports, and other materials related to the audit matters.
Where the party subject to enforcement conceals audit materials, the People's Court may take search measures according to law.

Article 19: Where the party subject to enforcement refuses to provide, transfers, conceals, forges, alters, or destroys audit materials, obstructs auditors from viewing the business premises, or commits other acts hindering audit investigation, the People's Court may, depending on the seriousness of the circumstances, impose a fine or detention on the party subject to enforcement or its principal person in charge or directly responsible personnel; if the conduct constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 20: The audit fees shall be prepaid by the applicant for enforcement who applies for the audit. Where the party subject to enforcement has refused to report or falsely reported property, concealed or transferred property, or had other circumstances of evading debts, the audit fees shall be borne by the party subject to enforcement; where no such circumstances of the party subject to enforcement are found, the audit fees shall be borne by the applicant for enforcement.

Article 22: Where the People's Court decides to search for property by reward, it shall make a reward announcement. The reward announcement shall specify the amount of the reward or the method of calculation, the conditions for claiming the reward, and other contents.
The reward announcement shall be published on the national court enforcement reward announcement platform, court microblogs, WeChat, or other media platforms, and may also be posted on the bulletin board of the enforcement court or at the domicile or habitual residence of the party subject to enforcement. Where the applicant for enforcement applies to publish on other media platforms and voluntarily bears the publishing costs, the People's Court shall permit it.

Article 23: After the reward announcement is published, if relevant personnel provide property leads to the People's Court, the People's Court shall register the identity information of the relevant personnel and the property leads; where two or more persons provide the same property leads, they shall be registered in the order in which the leads were provided.
The People's Court shall keep confidential the identity information of the relevant personnel and the property leads, except where it is necessary to inform the applicant for enforcement for the purpose of paying the reward.

Article 24: Where relevant personnel provide property leads not yet known to the People's Court and thereby realize in whole or in part the claim of the applicant for enforcement who applied for the issuance of the reward announcement, the People's Court shall pay the reward in accordance with the reward announcement.
The reward shall be deducted from the enforcement proceeds to which the applicant for enforcement referred to in the preceding paragraph is entitled. Where enforcement involves delivery of specific property or there are other circumstances making deduction impossible, the reward shall be paid separately by such applicant for enforcement.
Where the relevant personnel is an agent of the applicant for enforcement, a person obligated to provide property leads to the People's Court, or other circumstances exist under which the reward shall not be paid, the reward shall not be paid.

Article 25: Enforcement personnel shall not investigate information irrelevant to the enforcement case, and shall keep confidential the state secrets, trade secrets, and personal privacy learned in the course of investigation.

Article 26: These Provisions shall come into force as of May 1, 2017.
After these Provisions come into force, where the judicial interpretations previously published by this Court are inconsistent with these Provisions, these Provisions shall prevail.
